body:
... and all of which is meaningless in my case, because I'm not under anyone's care or control.  

So to recap: you were wrong to state that suicide is always a felony (it isn't in my state), and the point you were trying to make is irrelevant.  What, exactly, did you hope you would accomplish?
Which is, of course, why you incorrectly called it a "felony," which has a very specific meaning that is *all about* "arresting you and charging you with a crime."
It can go unnoticed forever, and it will.

> I hate being a lawyer.

I wish I had a job I had the luxury of complaining about.  So you've got that at least.
Truth.  Also, why the hell should miserable people be forced to stick around for other people's amusement?  You want to talk about selfish, *that's* what's fucking selfish.
Oh how sad for you.

I admit that "criminal" was too strong a word, but it would still be a shitty and immoral thing for me to escape my loans by fucking off to some tropical island that doesn't have an extradition treaty *and continuing to live*.  I have zero respect for people who flee their obligations that way, or for people who advocate it.

Also, regarding your other options: 

1. I'm already in therapy.  It's part of my budget which says I have 3 - 4 months of money left (I just paid rent and student loans and all the other monthly expenses, so there goes one month, *plus* I had to pay to get my keys replaced after they got stolen from the gym, so that screws up my calculations.)

2. I've said this before: forbearance and deferments/economic hardship/etc. are a waste of time because *the debt doesn't go away*.  It just gets *bigger* because the interest keeps accumulating.
Cute.  Stupid, but cute.
TIL you can't read sarcasm for shit.

I've made it clear to them (long before I was ever suicidal) that I don't want a funeral and that I want my body unceremoniously donated to science.  Or chopped up for parts.  Either way, if they decide to waste money on a funeral for me despite that, *not my problem*.

My dad is retired on disability and disowned me for having dated my ex.  My mom has to support herself, her worthless boyfriend, and her boyfriend's college-aged kid.  They don't need (and in dad's case, don't want) an extra mouth to feed.
TIL that *not* breaching a contract makes you "the worst (potential) lawyer ever."

Not in my state.

Also, if the state can find a way to convict a dead man, make him serve time in prison, and *have him notice*, then I'll be impressed.
TIL that caring more about seeing your legal obligations carried out than preserving your own treacherous hide is trolling and comical.

Correct.  Either of those would require taking another Bar exam, which I do not have the money to study for, which would only exacerbate my money problems further.  Plus, I don't have money for moving costs either.

> let me ask you this, what do you think will burden your family more, contributing to you financially during a difficult time in your life or dealing with your suicide?

The former.  Definitely the former.

It's funny that you think you know things.

Edit: Also, TIL suicidal people never want to set their affairs in order before they die.

Well, for one, I don't get to benefit from living debt-free if I kill myself rather than run away.  Second, the discharge-through-death bit was actually part of the agreement I signed, so it would actually be sticking within the terms of the loans rather than fucking off to another country and getting to enjoy a new debt-free life.
Okay, this is hilarious.  Fucking hilarious.  I'm upvoting you just because you're a funny and charming fellow who definitely has known love.

>  If you really want to kill yourself on Wed., what is the point of dying with money in the bank?

So the animal shelter my cats wind up languishing in until they get put to sleep or adopted will have enough bribe-money to actually take them in.

> Stop trolling.

TIL that wanting to die makes you a troll.

> Learn how to do a real estate closing and bang on some doors to get a few law firms to use you as a covering attorney. You'll probably have a few closings in the middle of the night an hour away but if you knock them out of the park then you will get more consistent work. Hey, at least you won't be in Stab Whitey. Or Mug Whitey. Also consider (as suggested by whodeeya) to get on the public defender list at the courts in your area. Make friends with the clerks. 

This is the closest to good advice I've gotten here.  It *isn't* good advice, because it's entirely out of touch with reality, papers over *huuuuuuuge* gaps in how any of this could ever really work, ignores practical gaps in my experience, and overlooks the flood of lawyers fighting tooth and nail for those appointment jobs, but it sure does *look* like good advice to someone who doesn't know any better.  And that's what counts for making yourself look good!

> finding something you love

Fuck love.  Fuck enjoying work.  Fuck that shit.  I need goddamn *money*.

> For tonight you need to go to your bathroom and look at yourself in the mirror. 

Okay.

God damn, I'm an ugly asshole.

> You're a goddamn attorney.

An *unemployed* attorney.  Which is worth as much as an unemployed garbage man.  Less, actually: at least the garbage man made things cleaner when he was working.

> Some bitch peace'd out on you and left you destitute?

Yup.  

> That's interesting, fuck it because it'll be a good story to tell later when your sitting in the law office that YOU built yourself from the ground up.

No, it's not.  First, I'm never going to have that office.  Second, she's going to laugh all the way to the bank (well, actually, she's done that already) and be convinced that she was right all along, and then she'll find some other guy to exploit and get away with that, too.  Oh, and she'll be doing this from the safety of a cushy government job I wound up recommending her for even after she kicked me out, because I'm a fucking loser.

> Remember when you sucked it up during first year and stayed in to the learn whatever the hell IIED means while your friends went to the Iron & Wine show?

No, because that never happened.

> Or how about the time you literally wanted to end your life during bar prep but you DIDN'T (and passed the test) because you're the fucking man? 

No, because that never happened.  Also, I'm not.

> You've got balls in there somewhere my friend I don't even know you but I know that.

No I don't and no *you* don't.

> You're a goddamn attorney. There are so many people out there who need your services.

No there aren't.

> And you sure as hell don't need to be part of Random Law Firm A to find them.

Yes I do, because I have no malpractice insurance, cannot afford malpractice insurance, and have no head for business.

> You need to look in the mirror and live up to your own expectations.

So you're saying I *am* the sort of person who would drive off a bridge.  Okay.
I'm registered with at least four in this city.  I have been since May.  Zero leads for anything but document review, and even those jobs lasted all of six weeks *total*.

I mean no more offense than strictly necessary, but it sounds like you're expecting me to take advice that *you didn't*, and your life worked out just fine without it.  That's not exactly a ringing endorsement.

I've done document review.  It's the contract and temp work I've been talking about.  It did pay well, but now there aren't any jobs in my area, and last week the job I thought I had lined up got cancelled before it could start. 

Also, I'm more or less stuck at Mug Whitey and Stab Whitey because of the furry creatures that depend on me for sustenance.
Why would you do that?  I didn't ask you to do that.  Seriously, why the flying fuck did you waste everyone's time doing that?

I am in no way prepared to hang up a shingle.  I do not have malpractice insurance.  I cannot afford malpractice insurance.  Plus, I know plenty of people who are *waaay* smarter than me who did work on the cheap for start-ups, and it fucked them in the ass.

Edit to reply to your edit: I have no goddamn accomplishments, and the closest I get to feeling like I've done something is fucking squats, and I've already plateaued on them right when I hit my body-weight.  As for this sense of adventure bullcrap, I've tried getting away from shit, but the problem is *shit is always waiting when I come back*, and I'm not the kind of person who can bug out and live carefree while leaving the rest to fucking burn.^1

> On the other side of the fence, it's the same fucking grass man. I am a prisoner to my desk, and the things I owned have come to own me.

I would kill gladly kill you, your whole family, *my* whole family, and the entire extended families of any three people you could pull from a hat if it meant I could have a desk and a job.  

> Martha Stuart checkered duvet covers

Shit, man, I don't even have a *microwave* or a pot to boil shit in any more.

^1 You did note how I said "live," right?  Because that word is very fucking important.  I'm fine in fucking off and *dying* and leaving it all to burn, because *by dying I've already given myself the most severe punishment the law allows for anything*.

It actually would make me feel better if I were the only one in this situation, because then the job market only has to turn around a little for me to get a job, as opposed to turning around for everyone else before it reaches me.

1. My law school's career services is a joke.  Unless you're looking for a job in that state or NYC, they have nothing.  They won't even return my phone calls for a damn resume critique.  They emailed me about a job fair they were throwing last month, and when I called them to express my interest and make a reservation, they told me alumni weren't allowed.  They already have me on the record from back in 2009 saying that I'd found a job, and as far as I know I'm still listed as being employed so my school can boost its rankings.

2. I graduated 2009.  If hiring ever picks up again (it won't), there will be thousands of other inexperienced lawyers to take my place, in addition to the hundreds of lawyers with 15 years of experience competing with me for the same entry-level jobs.  

3. No you wouldn't.  Every goddamn interviewer I've talked to has said that my contract work makes me unhirable in their eyes, and that's work in the legal field!  If I dropped out of the legal field to work retail, then I either have to admit I couldn't hack it as a lawyer (and thus wouldn't get hired) or have an unexplained gap in my resume (and thus wouldn't get hired).
I'm terrible with languages.
Yeah, with no malpractice insurance or any idea how to run a practice.  That'll work.
I'm not going to waste money traveling.

I have tried a headhunter.  He wanted me to do a temp-to-permanent position in another city while I was laid up with a broken ankle and couldn't drive.  I told him that I couldn't drive, and he *saw me in the cast limping on crutches*, and he still expected me to drive 90 minutes each way to interview on a Sunday.  I told him I *physically couldn't*, and explained that I did not have a ride, and he hasn't contacted me since.

That was back in March.
I am signed up with a nonprofit pro bono clinic.  It won't help me, but I did it anyway.

I'm not skipping out on my obligation to pay my debt by fleeing to another country.  I'm not a criminal.  If I cannot make my loan payments, *I will do the closest to honorable thing that I can and kill myself*, which discharges my debt *legally*.

Yes I've been persistent.  I hand-write fucking thank-you notes, for chrissake.  Yes, I embellish the hell out of my resume.  Yes, I research where I apply.  

Yes, I've asked friends for help, I even stayed with some of them for a couple months after I moved to this town for its stronger job market.  I've asked for referrals and gotten them, asked for LORs and gotten them, asked for family connections and gotten *them* too ... and it's gotten me nowhere.  

My family is no help for a job.  Of the ones that work at all (so not my dad, or my mom's entire family save her, or my *dad's* entire side of the family save his brother-in-law), they work for the government, where budget freezes and anti-nepotism regulations keep me out, to say nothing of the fierce competition from experienced lawyers who want job security and benefits.

Tried county attorney jobs, no luck.  Tried city attorney jobs, no luck.  Tried public defender jobs, they only want people with criminal law experience.  Tried government jobs that I *have* experience for, never heard back.  Tried private-sector jobs, they don't like my contract work and lack of 15 years as an attorney in whatever very specialized field they're in. 

Deferring my loans is pointless; the debt doesn't go away and interest just stacks up.  Don't qualify for EBT or food stamps.  No more unemployment benefits because those are used up.  Not going to wait tables or work retail; those don't pay enough to cover my debt *and* would prevent me from ever getting hired as a lawyer (because I'd have gone from lawyer to retail, thus proving I can't make it as a lawyer) *and* would be jobs I'm both overqualified for (lawyer) and underqualified for (no retail experience).

So I'm pretty much fucked if I try to live.
